question: For each cell of Q x R x W, what is identifiable, from what evidence and assumptions, at what sample or experiment cost, and what is the best known bound or impossibility result?

schema.question: Q: skeleton | orientation | effects | experiment design | confidence
schema.regime: R: D, D+I (hard/soft, known/unknown targets), D+K (type), D+I+K
schema.world_assumptions: W: sufficiency, functional form, faithfulness variant, time, cycles, dimension, data type
schema.identifiable_object: what is identified in the population (CPDAG, I-essential graph, MPDAG, PAG, full DAG, effect set)
schema.reference: author, year, venue (venue marked unconfirmed where not seen on the page)
schema.finite_sample_or_rate: rate or finite-sample statement if known

rows.question: skeleton
rows.world_assumptions: causally sufficient, iid, acyclic; Markov + adjacency-faithfulness; nonparametric CI tests
rows.key_result: Two DAGs are observationally equivalent iff they share skeleton and v-structures, so the skeleton is identified under faithfulness; PC is pointwise consistent. CPC (Ramsey et al.) needs only adjacency-faithfulness for correct adjacencies.
rows.reference: Verma & Pearl 1990 (UAI; arXiv 1304.1108); Ramsey, Zhang, Spirtes 2006 (UAI; arXiv 1206.6843)
rows.finite_sample_or_rate: pointwise only under plain faithfulness (see C05)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: No uniformly consistent skeleton estimator under plain faithfulness when time order is unknown (Robins et al. 2003; Zhang & Spirtes 2003).
rows.open_problems: Finite-sample skeleton guarantees without strong faithfulness.
rows.evidence_label: reported (skeleton+v-structure criterion is the standard statement; not confirmed in the Verma-Pearl abstract I read)
rows.read_level: abstract; CPC from project note cluster3

rows.question: orientation
rows.world_assumptions: causally sufficient, iid, acyclic; Markov + faithfulness (adjacency + orientation)
rows.key_result: Meek rules R1-R3 applied to the pattern give the maximally oriented graph (Meek 1995, Thm 3); GES identifies the class in the large-sample limit when a perfect DAG map exists (Chickering 2002).
rows.reference: Meek 1995 (UAI; arXiv 1302.4972); Chickering 2002 (JMLR 3:507-554)
rows.finite_sample_or_rate: none for orientation per se; orientation errors propagate through R1-R3
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: Edges inside undirected chain components of the CPDAG are not identifiable from D under any sample size.
rows.open_problems: Rates for orientation (vs skeleton) recovery; how often orientation-faithfulness fails at finite n.

rows.question: orientation
rows.world_assumptions: causally sufficient DAGs, uniform over classes
rows.identifiable_object: CPDAG size / share of compelled edges
rows.key_result: Sizes of MECs can be counted for sparse DAGs with hundreds of nodes; most classes are 'half completed' (partly oriented) with small average size; sparse class sizes grow roughly exponentially in p.
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: Share of non-compelled edges is a hard ceiling for D-only orientation.
rows.open_problems: Distribution of MEC sizes for the graph families used in benchmarks (project measured 91.8% compelled on CausalArena semantic).

rows.question: skeleton+orientation
rows.world_assumptions: Gaussian, causally sufficient, p = O(n^a), max neighbourhood q = O(n^{1-b}), nonzero partial correlations >= c_n with 1/c_n = O(n^d), d < b/2
rows.key_result: PC recovers the skeleton (and the CPDAG) with probability 1 - O(exp(-C n^{1-2d})).
rows.reference: Kalisch & Buehlmann 2007 (JMLR 8:613-636; arXiv math/0510436)
rows.finite_sample_or_rate: P(error) = O(exp(-C n^{1-2d})) under the c_n lower bound (a strong-faithfulness-type condition)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: The c_n condition fails with non-trivial probability for random parameters (C06).
rows.open_problems: Rates under weaker faithfulness.

rows.question: skeleton / effects
rows.world_assumptions: Markov + plain faithfulness; time order unknown and/or latent confounders
rows.key_result: Under Markov + faithfulness, tests and estimators are pointwise but not uniformly consistent; no finite n guarantees approximate correctness, and no valid consistent confidence intervals exist. With an observed discrete confounder and known order, uniformly consistent tests exist.
rows.reference: Robins, Scheines, Spirtes, Wasserman 2003 (Biometrika 90(3):491-515); Zhang & Spirtes 2003 (UAI)
rows.experiment_cost: randomised experiment restores uniform consistency (Robins et al., Remark 3)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: IMPOSSIBILITY: no uniformly consistent test/estimator/confidence map (Thms 1,3,4); extends to inferring time order (Thm 5); Gaussian case: no nontrivial uniformly consistent test (Thm 6).
rows.open_problems: Which minimal strengthening (k-triangle, strong faithfulness, order knowledge) is credible in a given domain.

rows.question: skeleton+orientation
rows.world_assumptions: linear Gaussian, causally sufficient; lambda-strong-faithfulness with lambda ~ sqrt(deg log p / n); edge weights uniform on [-1,1], unit error variances
rows.key_result: The set of non-strong-faithful distributions has positive measure and is often large: lower bounds 1-(1-lambda)^{p-1} for trees, exponential in p^2 for cycles, in 2^p for bipartite K_{2,p-2}. Simulated 10-node DAGs (expected degree 2): share lambda-strong-unfaithful nearly 1 at lambda=0.1, ~0.9 at 0.01, ~0.7 at 0.001.
rows.reference: Uhler, Raskutti, Buehlmann, Yu 2013 (Ann. Statist.; DOI 10.1214/12-AOS1080; arXiv 1207.0547)
rows.finite_sample_or_rate: For the lower bound to vanish need p_n = o(sqrt(n/(deg log n))) (trees), o((n/(deg log n))^{1/4}) (cycles), o(log n) (bipartite)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: Authors conclude high-dimensional PC consistency 'seems rather unrealistic' under uniform parameters; even trees cannot have p >> n.
rows.open_problems: Tightness of bounds; non-uniform parameter priors; discrete data.

rows.question: skeleton+orientation
rows.world_assumptions: linear Gaussian, causally sufficient; k-Triangle-Faithfulness (weaker than strong faithfulness)
rows.key_result: A uniformly consistent estimator of the MEC and of identifiable coefficients exists under Markov + k-Triangle-Faithfulness; strong faithfulness 'may be false with high probability'.
rows.reference: Spirtes & Zhang 2014 (Statist. Sci. 29(4); arXiv 1502.00829)
rows.finite_sample_or_rate: uniform consistency (no explicit rate in abstract)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: Robins et al. impossibility under plain faithfulness is the backdrop.
rows.open_problems: Credibility of k-triangle-faithfulness on real data.

rows.question: skeleton+orientation
rows.key_result: No algorithm converges for all networks; any algorithm achieving the best achievable mode of convergence must converge on all faithful networks, so assuming faithfulness is 'a requirement, not an option'. Sparsest-permutation methods are consistent under conditions strictly weaker than faithfulness.
rows.reference: Lin & Zhang 2020 (ALT, PMLR 117:554-582); Raskutti & Uhler (arXiv 1307.0366)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: No universally convergent learner exists.
rows.open_problems: Finite-sample versions of the convergence-mode hierarchy.

rows.question: skeleton (CI testing)
rows.key_result: A valid conditional independence test has no power against any alternative; finite-sample validity requires restricting the null (e.g. regression rate assumptions, as in the GCM).
rows.reference: Shah & Peters 2020 (Ann. Statist.; DOI 10.1214/19-AOS1857; arXiv 1804.07203)
rows.finite_sample_or_rate: rates only under assumptions on regression estimators
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: NO-FREE-LUNCH: every constraint-based guarantee inherits assumptions on the CI tests.
rows.open_problems: Practical test choice for mixed/nonlinear data at n=1000.

rows.question: skeleton+orientation
rows.key_result: GES and adaptively restricted GES (ARGES) are consistent in several sparse high-dimensional settings; simulations favour them over PC.
rows.reference: Nandy, Hauser, Maathuis 2018 (Ann. Statist. 46(6A); arXiv 1507.02608)
rows.finite_sample_or_rate: consistency (conditions in full text, not read)
rows.open_problems: Explicit rates for GES.

rows.question: full graph
rows.world_assumptions: Bayesian networks, m variables, max in-degree k
rows.key_result: Exact structure recovery needs Omega(m) samples for non-sparse BNs and Omega(k log m + k^2/m) for sparse BNs.
rows.reference: Ghoshal & Honorio (arXiv 1601.07460; venue not confirmed)
rows.finite_sample_or_rate: LOWER BOUND Omega(k log m + k^2/m)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: Lower bound holds for any method.
rows.open_problems: Matching upper bounds for faithfulness-based methods.

rows.question: full graph
rows.world_assumptions: linear, acyclic, non-Gaussian errors, no hidden confounders
rows.key_result: LiNGAM identifies the complete causal structure from observational data without a time order.
rows.reference: Shimizu, Hoyer, Hyvarinen, Kerminen 2006 (JMLR 7:2003-2030)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: Gaussian errors -> back to MEC.
rows.open_problems: Behaviour when errors are near-Gaussian at n=1000.

rows.question: full graph
rows.world_assumptions: additive noise models (nonlinear f, additive noise), causal minimality, no hidden confounders
rows.key_result: Bivariate ANMs are identifiable except when a differential-equation condition fails (linear-Gaussian is the classic exception); restricted multivariate ANMs identify the DAG (Thm 27); nonlinear Gaussian ANMs identifiable (Cor 30).
rows.reference: Hoyer et al. 2008 (NIPS 21); Peters, Mooij, Janzing, Schoelkopf 2014 (JMLR 15:2009-2053)
rows.finite_sample_or_rate: no rate in what I read
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: Non-identifiable cases fall into five classes (Prop 22).
rows.open_problems: Robustness to misspecification and finite-sample independence tests.

rows.question: full graph
rows.key_result: PNL is identifiable in most cases; the non-identifiable cases are enumerated.
rows.reference: Zhang & Hyvarinen 2009 (UAI; arXiv 1205.2599; PMLR r7)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: Enumerated exceptional cases.
rows.open_problems: Multivariate PNL identifiability in practice.

rows.question: full graph
rows.world_assumptions: linear Gaussian SEM with equal (or known-ratio) error variances
rows.key_result: Equal error variances make the DAG identifiable (Peters & Buehlmann); with error variances known up to a constant, the true DAG uniquely minimises a reweighted l2 score (Loh & Buehlmann). Optimal sample complexity n ~ q log(d/q).
rows.reference: Peters & Buehlmann 2014 (Biometrika; arXiv 1205.2536); Loh & Buehlmann 2014 (JMLR 15:3065-3105); Gao, Tai, Aragam (arXiv 2201.10548)
rows.finite_sample_or_rate: minimax n ~ q log(d/q) (Gao et al. Thms 2.1, 3.1)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: Lower bound max{log d / beta_min^2, q log(d/q)/(M^2-1)} (Gao et al. Thm 3.1).
rows.open_problems: Assumption is exactly what varsortability exploits in simulated benchmarks (Reisach et al. 2021); fails after standardisation.

rows.question: full graph
rows.world_assumptions: linear (Gaussian or not), known topological order, sparse
rows.key_result: With the order known, DAG estimation reduces to per-node variable selection; adaptive lasso is consistent; best-subset selection attains n ~ q log(d/q) with a matching lower bound (Gao et al. Props 4.1-4.2).
rows.reference: Shojaie & Michailidis 2010 (Biometrika 97(3):519-538); Gao, Tai, Aragam (arXiv 2201.10548, Sec. 4)
rows.finite_sample_or_rate: n ~ q log(d/q), same as undirected graphical-model selection
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: Lower bound matches (Prop 4.2).
rows.open_problems: Rates with a noisy or partially known order.

rows.question: orientation
rows.key_result: Meek rules R1-R4 after imposing the knowledge give the maximally oriented graph (Meek 1995, Thm 4); MPDAGs support reading possible ancestry, an adjustment criterion and IDA; effects become more identifiable with more knowledge (simulation).
rows.reference: Meek 1995 (UAI; arXiv 1302.4972); Perkovic, Kalisch, Maathuis 2017 (UAI; arXiv 1707.02171)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: Knowledge inconsistent with the CPDAG is not handled.
rows.open_problems: Soft/erroneous knowledge with guarantees.

rows.question: orientation
rows.key_result: All cross-tier edges are directed; only Meek R1 is needed to complete; result is a chain graph with chordal components so CPDAG adjustment and IDA apply unchanged; fully shielded within-tier edges stay undirected; tiers give absence, never presence, of ancestral relations; earlier knowledge is more informative.
rows.reference: Bang & Didelez 2023 (UAI, PMLR 216:119-129; arXiv 2306.01638)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: A complete subgraph inside one tier cannot be oriented by tiers (Example 5).
rows.open_problems: PAG extension is a conjecture (needs no cross-tier confounding, no selection); erroneous tiers.

rows.question: orientation / effects
rows.identifiable_object: causal MPDAG + residual direct causal clauses
rows.key_result: Any pairwise causal knowledge set decomposes uniquely into a causal MPDAG plus a minimal residual set of direct causal clauses; consistency/equivalence checks are polynomial; effect identifiability depends only on the MPDAG (necessary and sufficient condition).
rows.reference: Fang, Zhao, Liu, He 2025 (JMLR 26:229); Fang & He 2020 (UAI, PMLR 124:270-279)
rows.open_problems: Ancestral knowledge is not representable by edge orientations alone (residual clauses).

rows.question: full graph
rows.identifiable_object: graph consistent with the partial order
rows.key_result: Partial orders are mapped to equivalent graph-space constraints with claimed correctness and completeness; reported 90% fewer samples on one real dataset.
rows.reference: Ban et al. 2024 (NeurIPS 2024 poster)
rows.open_problems: No identifiability theorem beyond constraint equivalence in what I read.

rows.question: orientation
rows.key_result: FCI with tiered background knowledge is sound and complete; for other knowledge types it is not known when FCI stays complete. Local background knowledge also has sound and complete rules (Wang, Qin, Zhou).
rows.reference: Andrews, Spirtes, Cooper 2020 (AISTATS, PMLR 108:4002-4011); Wang, Qin, Zhou 2022 (NeurIPS 35)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: Completeness of FCI under general (non-tiered) knowledge is open.
rows.open_problems: Selection bias with tiers not confirmed in what I read.

rows.question: orientation
rows.world_assumptions: latent confounders and selection bias, acyclic, Markov + faithfulness
rows.key_result: FCI with added rules is complete: it recovers every feature uniquely determined by conditional independence facts; Zhang's tail rules complete the MAG-equivalence commonalities.
rows.reference: Zhang 2008 (Artificial Intelligence 172(16-17):1873-1896); Zhang (arXiv 1206.5282)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: No uniformly consistent procedure (Robins et al. 2003).
rows.open_problems: Finite-sample PAG accuracy; FCI recall on autocorrelated data (see C38).

rows.question: full graph
rows.key_result: With latent confounders uniqueness is lost but at most a finite set of models fits the data.
rows.reference: Hoyer, Shimizu, Kerminen 2006 (arXiv cs/0603038)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: Non-uniqueness.

rows.question: skeleton (selection)
rows.world_assumptions: selection bias, parametric and non-parametric families
rows.key_result: Conditions under which selection bias is identifiable from observational data are given, with tests for its presence.
rows.reference: Kaltenpoth & Vreeken 2023 (AAAI 37(7):8177-8185)
rows.open_problems: Combining detection with PAG learning.

rows.question: orientation
rows.key_result: Interventional equivalence partitions DAGs more finely than observational; each class is represented by a chain graph (I-essential graph); GES generalises (GIES).
rows.reference: Hauser & Buehlmann 2012 (JMLR 13:2409-2464)

rows.question: orientation
rows.key_result: Characterises the I-MEC identifiable from general (not necessarily perfect) interventions and gives a provably consistent algorithm.
rows.reference: Yang, Katcoff, Uhler 2018 (ICML, PMLR 80:5541-5550)

rows.question: orientation
rows.key_result: Characterises the class identifiable from mixed observational/interventional data with partly or fully unknown targets; consistent permutation search (UT-IGSP). JCI handles unknown targets/types by context variables.
rows.reference: Squires, Wang, Uhler 2020 (UAI, PMLR 124:1039-1048); Mooij, Magliacane, Claassen 2020 (JMLR 21:99)

rows.question: orientation
rows.key_result: Psi-Markov property; graphical equivalence test via augmented MAGs (skeleton, unshielded colliders, discriminating paths); Psi-FCI sound and complete in the sample limit.
rows.reference: Jaber, Kocaoglu, Shanmugam, Bareinboim 2020 (NeurIPS 33)

rows.question: experiment design
rows.key_result: With unrestricted simultaneous randomisation, log2(N)+1 experiments are sufficient and in the worst case necessary; single-variable experiments need N-1.
rows.reference: Eberhardt, Glymour, Scheines 2005 (UAI; arXiv 1207.1389)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: worst-case necessary
rows.read_level: abstract (bounded-k formula partly garbled in extraction)

rows.question: experiment design
rows.key_result: ceil(log2 omega(G)) unbounded-size targets suffice and are worst-case necessary, omega = largest clique of undirected components (proves Eberhardt's conjecture); OptUnb finds them in polynomial time; a greedy single-vertex strategy is also given.
rows.reference: Hauser & Buehlmann 2014 (IJAR; DOI 10.1016/j.ijar.2013.11.007; arXiv 1205.4174); Eberhardt 2008 (UAI; arXiv 1206.3250)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: worst-case necessary

rows.question: experiment design
rows.key_result: Any deterministic adaptive algorithm must be a separating system on complete graphs in the worst case; near-optimal separating systems; adaptive algorithm on chordal skeletons is an alpha-approximation (alpha = independence number).
rows.reference: Shanmugam, Kocaoglu, Dimakis, Vishwanath 2015 (NIPS; arXiv 1511.00041)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: information-theoretic lower bound also for randomized adaptive

rows.question: experiment design
rows.key_result: Universal lower bound: at least the sum over chain components of half the largest clique size; DCT policy within a log factor (in number of maximal cliques) of optimal; an improved universal lower bound within factor 2 of optimal.
rows.reference: Squires et al. 2020 (arXiv 2011.00641; venue not confirmed); Porwal, Srivastava, Sinha 2022 (AISTATS, PMLR 151:5583-5603)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: LOWER BOUND, within factor 2 of optimum

rows.question: experiment design
rows.key_result: Minimal verifying set characterised via covered edges; separator-based adaptive search uses O(log n) times the verification number, which is tight (Omega(log n) on some graphs); O(log n log k) for size-k interventions.
rows.reference: Choo, Shiragur, Bhattacharyya 2022 (NeurIPS 2022; arXiv 2206.15374)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: Omega(log n) worst-case ratio

rows.question: experiment design
rows.regime: D+I (orient a target subset of edges)
rows.key_result: Subset verification computable efficiently; for subset search no algorithm beats a ratio of the target edges' vertex cover in the worst case.
rows.reference: Choo & Shiragur (arXiv 2301.03180; venue not confirmed)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: vertex-cover-sized gap is unavoidable
rows.open_problems: Question-driven (effect-targeted) design bounds.

rows.question: experiment design
rows.key_result: Minimum-cost intervention set identifying any DAG with a given skeleton is polynomial-time; with a capped number, poly-time for trees/clique trees, greedy for chordal. Budgeted k single-target non-adaptive design: objective (expected oriented edges) is submodular, greedy gives (1-1/e).
rows.reference: Kocaoglu, Dimakis, Vishwanath 2017 (ICML, PMLR 70:1875-1884); Ghassami, Salehkaleybar, Kiyavash, Bareinboim 2018 (ICML, PMLR 80:1724-1733)

rows.question: experiment design
rows.key_result: O(d log^2 n + d^2 log n) interventions learn the graph with latents (d = degree), versus O(n^2) naive.
rows.reference: Kocaoglu, Shanmugam, Bareinboim 2017 (NIPS 30)
rows.experiment_cost: O(d log^2 n + d^2 log n)

rows.question: full graph / experiment design
rows.key_result: Necessary and sufficient conditions on the set of experiments for identifiability are given.
rows.reference: Hyttinen, Eberhardt, Hoyer 2012 (JMLR 13:3387-3439)
rows.experiment_cost: set of experiments satisfying the paper's condition (not read)

rows.question: full graph (lagged)
rows.world_assumptions: Granger: complete system, no unmeasured confounders, no instantaneous effects, sampling at causal lag, no measurement error
rows.key_result: Granger causality assesses predictiveness; it matches causal structure only under the listed assumptions, which the review calls unverifiable and unlikely to hold together; sub-sampling can make effects unidentifiable and create spurious ones.
rows.reference: Shojaie & Fox 2022 (Annu. Rev. Stat. Appl. 9:289-319; arXiv 2105.02675)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: Omitted variables can reverse Granger conclusions (review's simulation).

rows.question: full graph (lagged + contemporaneous)
rows.key_result: PCMCI is consistent for lagged links with no contemporaneous effects; finite-sample false-positive control is empirical. PCMCI+ handles contemporaneous links, order-independent and oracle-consistent.
rows.reference: Runge et al. 2019 (Sci. Adv.; arXiv 1702.07007); Runge 2020 (UAI; arXiv 2003.03685)

rows.question: orientation
rows.key_result: LPCMCI is order-independent and sound and complete in the oracle case, with much higher recall than FCI variants on autocorrelated data; SVAR-FCI style methods allow contemporaneous relations and latent processes.
rows.reference: Gerhardus & Runge 2020 (NeurIPS 33); Malinsky & Spirtes 2018 (KDD workshop, PMLR 92:23-47)

rows.question: full graph
rows.world_assumptions: restricted SEMs (independent noise, e.g. additive) or non-Gaussian SVAR
rows.key_result: TiMINo identifies lagged and instantaneous effects, possibly nonlinear and unfaithful, and non-instantaneous feedback; non-Gaussian SVAR is identifiable without prior structure knowledge.
rows.reference: Peters, Janzing, Schoelkopf 2013 (NIPS 26); Hyvarinen, Zhang, Shimizu, Hoyer 2010 (JMLR 11:1709-1731)

rows.question: full graph
rows.identifiable_object: set of system-timescale structures consistent with data
rows.key_result: Constraint satisfaction/optimisation recovers system-timescale structures consistent with the measured-timescale graph, robust to statistical conflicts.
rows.reference: Hyttinen, Plis, Jarvisalo, Eberhardt, Danks 2016 (PGM, PMLR 52:216-227)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: Generally not unique (equivalence set; details not read).

rows.question: orientation
rows.key_result: Conditions under which micro-level edges can be oriented using a summary causal graph, including macro-level cycles or bidirected edges.
rows.reference: Loranchet & Assaad (arXiv 2508.21742; 2025-2026 preprint)

rows.question: orientation
rows.key_result: FCI output stays correct with feedback: sound and complete for observational data from simple sigma-faithful SCMs; consistent for presence/absence of (direct) causal relations, absence of confounders and of specific cycles. Cyclic SCMs may lack solutions or unique distributions unless solvability holds.
rows.reference: Mooij & Claassen 2020 (UAI; arXiv 2005.00610); Bongers, Forre, Peters, Mooij 2021 (Ann. Statist. 49(5))
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: Cyclic SCMs need not satisfy a Markov property without solvability.

rows.question: full graph
rows.key_result: LiNG-D outputs the distribution equivalence class; under sufficient conditions only one member is stable.
rows.reference: Lacerda, Spirtes, Ramsey, Hoyer 2008 (UAI; arXiv 1206.3273)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: Non-unique in general.

rows.question: full graph
rows.world_assumptions: linear mixed continuous/discrete (LiM); ordinal + exponential family linear models
rows.key_result: LiM is identifiable under sufficient conditions; for ordered-logit and one-parameter exponential-family nodes, every ordinal-to-EF edge direction is identifiable given >=3 categories and >=3 support points, both necessary.
rows.reference: Zeng, Shimizu, Matsui, Sun 2022 (CLeaR, PMLR 177:994-1009); Mishra & Mitra (arXiv 2609.17942, Sept 2026 preprint)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: Necessity of the 3-category / 3-point conditions (Mishra & Mitra).
rows.open_problems: Nonparametric mixed data: identifiable object stays the CPDAG; validity rests on mixed CI tests (C09).

rows.question: effects P(Y|do(X))
rows.identifiable_object: multiset of possible effects; identification status per (X,Y)
rows.key_result: IDA returns one effect per allowed parent set of X (min |effect| is a lower bound); the generalized adjustment criterion is sound and complete for DAGs, CPDAGs, MAGs, PAGs; an optimal (minimum asymptotic variance) adjustment set exists for linear models in DAGs/CPDAGs/MPDAGs.
rows.reference: Maathuis, Kalisch, Buehlmann 2009 (Ann. Statist. 37(6A); arXiv 0810.4214); Perkovic, Textor, Kalisch, Maathuis 2018 (JMLR 18:220); Henckel, Perkovic, Maathuis 2022 (JRSSB; arXiv 1907.02435)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: Effect not identifiable when X has undirected edges whose orientation changes the parent set.

rows.question: effects P(Y|do(X))
rows.key_result: Necessary and sufficient identification criterion in MPDAGs, generalising the g-formula/truncated factorisation; strictly stronger than generalized adjustment. Local IDA with direct-causal knowledge; tiered MPDAGs keep CPDAG adjustment and IDA unchanged.
rows.reference: Perkovic 2020 (UAI, PMLR 124:530-539); Fang & He 2020 (UAI); Bang & Didelez 2023 (Cor 2-3)

rows.question: effects P(Y|do(X))
rows.identifiable_object: identified expression or proof of non-identifiability; bounds
rows.key_result: Complete identification algorithm given a PAG (returns an expression or certifies non-identifiability). LV-IDA returns multisets with NA where confounding cannot be ruled out; min/max bound the effect when identifiable.
rows.reference: Jaber, Zhang, Bareinboim 2019 (ICML, PMLR 97:2981-2989); Malinsky & Spirtes 2016 (CMU tech report 194 / PGM 2016)
rows.finite_sample_or_rate: LV-IDA sim, 15 vars: MSE 0.022 vs IDA 0.056; 12.7% NA (reported)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: With latents, no uniformly consistent effect estimator or CI (Robins et al. 2003).

rows.question: graph-feature confidence
rows.key_result: Bootstrap frequencies rank features but are not calibrated probabilities; Bayesian model averaging over orders gives posterior feature probabilities; BCCD and ACI attach reliability/confidence to causal statements.
rows.reference: Friedman, Goldszmidt, Wyner 1999 (UAI; arXiv 1301.6695); Friedman & Koller 2000 (UAI; arXiv 1301.3856); Claassen & Heskes (arXiv 1210.4866); Magliacane, Claassen, Mooij 2016 (NIPS 29)
rows.finite_sample_or_rate: plain bootstrap ECE ~0.07-0.08 (second-hand, project note cluster6, Banerjee et al. 2025)
rows.impossibility_or_lower_bound: No coverage or calibration guarantee; posterior validity depends on model and prior.
rows.open_problems: Calibration at scenario-level n~25 (project DOM-08).

rows.question: skeleton (error control)
rows.key_result: PC-p computes edge-specific p-value upper bounds and controls FDR across edges with Benjamini-Yekutieli.
rows.reference: Strobl, Spirtes, Visweswaran 2019 (ACM TIST 10(5) per index; arXiv 1607.03975)
rows.open_problems: Orientation-level error control.

rows.question: orientation / effects (coverage)
rows.world_assumptions: linear equal-variance or identifiable additive-error SEMs
rows.identifiable_object: confidence sets of orderings / effects including structure uncertainty
rows.key_result: Test inversion gives confidence regions for effects covering structure uncertainty (two-step intervals are over-optimistic); residual-bootstrap confidence sets of causal orderings are asymptotically valid and yield sub/supersets of ancestral relations.

rows.question: effects after discovery
rows.identifiable_object: valid CI for effect after selecting graph
rows.key_result: Double dipping inflates miscoverage; resampling-and-screening over perturbed PC runs gives asymptotically correct coverage for the fixed population effect; Gradu et al. give valid post-discovery inference beating data splitting.
rows.reference: Chang, Guo, Malinsky (arXiv 2405.06763); Gradu, Zrnic, Wang, Jordan (arXiv 2208.05949; JASA 120(550) per RePEc)

rows.question: effects (conformal)
rows.key_result: Conformal guarantee covers a posterior-weighted pseudo-outcome over candidate DAGs, not the effect or the graph; effect coverage is empirical (>90% on five benchmarks).
rows.reference: Singh et al. (CausalGuard, arXiv 2605.21928, May 2026 preprint)
rows.open_problems: No conformal guarantee on graph features found.

rows.question: orientation (interventions, large graphs)
rows.world_assumptions: epsilon-interventional faithfulness, latents allowed, random ER / scale-free graphs
rows.key_result: False-negative rate concentrates at O(log d / sqrt(d)) on sparse ER DAGs.
